newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian minister happy to see GST debate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian minister happy to see GST debate.

text.p: Senior Australian minister Robert Hill said on Thursday a consumption tax might some day be introduced to Australia and the government, ruling out such a move in its current term, was happy to encourage the debate.

"There may well be a time in the future when the community is more comfortable with a change in that direction and as a result you might see governments responding accordingly," said Hill, environment minister and government leader in the Senate.
"It remains a debate we are happy to encourage and change may occur in that direction sometime in the future," he told the Committee for Economic Development of Australia.
Economists and business groups have called for a value-added tax to be applied to all consumption, replacing the current mix of wholesale taxes and permitting a reduction in income tax rates.

Advocates of the consumption tax -- called a goods and services tax or GST -- say the top marginal income tax rate of 47 percent destroys the incentive to earn and creates too much incentive for tax avoidance.
But the ruling Liberal-National coalition promised not to introduce a GST when it won the 1996 election.
It had unexpectedly lost the 1993 poll when it proposed a GST and the government now government ministers invariably stick by last year's promise.
